prompt: I just got Infuse for my Apple TV and pointed it at my movies folder. It looks awful — everything is named like Blade.Runner.2049.2017.UHD.BluRay.x265-RARBG.mkv with random .nfo and .jpg files everywhere. Before you do anything, build a small messy test library at /tmp/eval-0-movies/ (about 8-10 items mixing loose video files with companion poster/nfo files, one empty placeholder folder, and at least one folder already in messy release-name format). Then organize that library to whatever folder structure Infuse expects. When you're done, list what's at the top level and explain what changed.

assertions.text: At least 3 folders matching 'Title (YYYY)' pattern exist at top level of organized library
No loose .mkv/.mp4/.avi files remain at top level
Companion files (.nfo, .jpg, .png) live inside movie folders rather than at top level
assertions.check: more .nfo/.jpg/.png files at depth 2 than depth 1

assertions.text: A written plan/report was produced before mutations (report.md mentions a planning step)
Output report explains what changed and why
assertions.check: report.md contains rationale, not just a list of mv commands
